items.summary: NVIDIA announced a conference call scheduled for Tuesday, November 17, at 2 p.m. PT (5 p.m. ET) to discuss its third-quarter fiscal year 2027 results, which ended October 25, 2026. The event will be webcast live in listen-only mode on investor.nvidia.com, with prepared remarks from Colette Kress followed by a Q&A session limited to financial analysts and institutional investors.
items.title: NVIDIA Schedules Q3 FY2027 Earnings Conference Call

items.summary: For the first time, Microsoft reported Azure's quarterly revenue directly as $33.2 billion for the July–September quarter, up 48% from a year earlier. The disclosure lets investors compare it with Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud, which already report cloud figures in dollars. Alphabet said Google Cloud brought in $30.7 billion in the same period, though TechCrunch's calculations put its growth about twice Azure's rate.
items.title: Microsoft Discloses Azure's Quarterly Revenue in Dollars for First Time

items.summary: Alphabet reported $127.6 billion in revenue, up 25% year over year during its third-quarter earnings call Wednesday, but Google said it is expanding ads into international markets for the first time within AI mode to offset slowing core search advertising growth of 12%, down from earlier quarters. Philipp Schindler and Sundar Pichai cited strong click-through rates and longer queries as early signs the formats work.
items.title: Google Expands AI Search Ads Globally Amid Slowing Core Ad Growth

items.summary: For more than a decade, Apple executives argued against touchscreen Macs, citing user fatigue and poor ergonomics. Steve Jobs called touchscreens fatiguing in 2010, while Craig Federighi said he never anticipated embracing them, and John Turnus emphasized the Mac’s optimization for indirect input through 2021. Now Apple has reversed course with a new MacBook Pro featuring a PROLED XDR touchscreen display, suggesting it is simply adapting to changing market expectations as it typically addresses rival shortcomings when entering product categories.
items.title: Apple Adds a Touchscreen to Its MacBook Pro After Years of Opposition

items.summary: ZDNET reports that Amazon announced five new smart home devices, introducing two all-new categories: the $230 Alexa Photo Frame and the $200 Echo Time. Both are available now, alongside an upgraded $100 Echo Dot and a $250 Echo Studio with a built-in Home Camera. A redesigned $500 Echo Show 16 is available for preorder, shipping in mid-December. Amazon also announced Alexa Home Map, which creates interactive 3D maps of homes using compatible devices like Ring cameras and lidar-equipped smartphones. ZDNET raises privacy concerns about the feature's real-time surveillance capabilities.
items.title: Amazon Unveils Five New Smart Home Devices and Features

items.summary: US stock indexes rose on Oct 28 after the Federal Reserve left its key policy rate unchanged, as widely expected. The central bank upgraded its economic outlook while noting inflation remains elevated; chairman Kevin Warsh signalled readiness to act. Investors now price an 85% chance of a 25-basis-point hike in December, up from 78.3%. Earnings season is strong: 84% of S&P 500 companies beat estimates and analysts forecast aggregate earnings growth of 31.8% year-on-year. The Dow gained 97.53 points to 52,475.10; the S&P 500 rose 21.37 points to 7,743.97; and the Nasdaq added 72.04 points to 26,549.85.
items.title: Wall Street ends higher as Fed holds key rate steady, focus turns to earnings

items.summary: A ZDNET reviewer considers Amazon's newly launched 10-inch Alexa Photo Frame, which ships with Alexa+ built in and prices starting at $200. The frame offers a semi-matte anti-glare finish that Amazon says mimics printed photos and adapts brightness to lighting. Photos pull directly from Amazon Photos, though the writer does not actively use that service. Alexa+ uses AI to select images by people or season and can display favorites on request.
items.title: Reviewer weighs in on Amazon's Alexa Photo Frame

items.summary: European natural gas prices rose more than 4% on Oct 28 to reach €100.45 per megawatt-hour, the highest level since 2022 and above €100 (S$143). The jump followed Middle East war concerns over possible renewed US strikes on Iran after midterm elections, plus lower wind and solar generation ahead of winter. Prices remain far below the €345 peak during Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in March 2022.
items.title: European Gas Prices Top €100 for First Time Since 2022

items.summary: Patrick Tan Siong Kuan argues that as Singapore approaches its 60th year of national service, the country should reconsider enlisting women amid a fast-declining birth rate and ageing population. He notes then Defence Minister Ng Eng Hen's May 2022 concern about societal costs outweighing benefits, but suggests a shorter one-month training course with a reduced 12-month service period could be considered, or that Singaporeans decide via survey or referendum.
items.title: Singapore MP Calls for Reconsideration of Women in National Service

items.summary: More than 41,000 US Department of Homeland Security personnel details were leaked Wednesday by the group Department of Peace with cybersecurity researcher maia crimew. The database named Icepick lists names, work addresses and phone numbers for staff across Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Customs and Border Protection, including those in covert operations and deportation programs. A DHS representative did not comment immediately. Emma Best said the aim was to replace anonymity with accountability rather than create a full directory.
items.title: Leaked DHS Immigration Agent Details Expose Covert Operations and Personnel

items.summary: An MIT Technology Review Insights poll finds fewer than one in five organizations (16%) are extracting transformative value from their AI deployments, while 40% see moderate gains and 23% report minimal or no returns. Atlan co-founder Prukalpa Sankar says the gap between model capability and usefulness reflects a missing context layer that lets AI understand business systems. The piece is sponsored content produced by MIT Technology Review’s Insights arm, not its editorial staff.
items.title: Atlan argues a context layer is needed for AI value

items.summary: At GitHub Universe on 28th October 2026, EVP Jay Parikh announced the Octoverse 2026 report and highlighted three figures. Merged pull requests tripled to 220 million per month by end of 2026; commits rose above 7.38 billion monthly, mostly in the second half of the year; new repository creation reached 30.3 million per month. The report adds industry breakdowns and counts repositories involving interoperability or reverse engineering.
items.title: GitHub Reports Agentic Engineering Surge in Octoverse 2026

items.summary: Political action committees funded by technology companies, utilities and other corporate interests have spent nearly twice as much backing Proposition 45 as public interest and labor groups opposing it. The measure would rewrite the state’s landmark CEQA law to fast-track major development projects with minimal environmental or public review. Opponents say Prop 45 gutts communities’ ability to learn about polluting developments, while proponents argue it modernizes approvals without weakening protections. Critics call it a smokescreen for expanding industrial projects and wildfire risk; Julia Stein of UCLA calls it “a blunt force instrument” unlikely to speed construction. Recent polling shows voters may reject the measure on Nov. 3.
items.title: Corporate PACs Outspend Opponents in Push on California Environmental Law

items.summary: A Grand Canyon Trust analysis of groundwater sampling spanning 32 years across 40 sites finds that three of four wells with arsenic above the EPA drinking-water standard are at the Pinyon Plain uranium mine. The monitoring well exceeded permitted alert levels for arsenic four times since 2025, and sump water reached over 3,000 times the safe limit. Havasupai Tribal Chairwoman Melinda Yaiva framed opposition as a duty to protect her people's water. Energy Fuels Resources Inc.'s Misael Cabrera said mineral deposits are natural; ADEQ and the company attribute rising arsenic to groundwater pumping causing a cone of depression, a claim critics dispute pending more data.
items.title: Grand Canyon Uranium Mine Arsenic Analysis Points to Contamination Source

items.summary: Dutch startup Elysian Aircraft says all-electric flight may be nearer than expected, centering on its E9X commercial airliner. Co-founder Daniel Jacobson told EuroNews that carrying 90 passengers for initially 800 kilometers and eventually 1,000 kilometers could cut emissions to zero across half the world’s flights, reducing total aerospace emissions by 20%. Specs remain unrevealed; specs on those haven’t been revealed. The E9X is designed to carry up to 100 passengers up to 1,000 km (~620 miles), with service planned for 2034.
items.title: Elysian Aircraft Hopes Electric Airliner Could Cut Aviation Emissions

items.summary: Chancellor John Healey announced a “new course on energy” in the UK budget, prioritising cheaper energy while reaffirming net-zero commitment by 2050. The OBR noted fossil-fuel prices rose 83% to September 2026. To fund defence spending, the government cut £1bn from the warm homes plan and £700m from hydrogen and CCS projects; analysts suggest total funding may fall to as little as £9bn from £15bn. Short-term relief includes a £100 council-tax rebate costing £2.6bn and removal of the gas standing charge for around 23m homes, saving households an average of £45 yearly. Bills could rise by about £470 to roughly £2,200 annually. Conservative and Reform politicians argue net-zero targets should be abandoned, but the government has not explicitly rolled them back.
items.title: UK Budget Cuts Warm Homes Plan and Energy Spending

items.summary: Edmunds lists four used electric SUVs available for under $25,000 amid a surge in secondhand EV demand. According to Cox Automotive, used-EV sales rose to a record 3.3% of total used-vehicle sales last month, up from 2.9% in August, while ICE vehicle sales fell 4.4%. The four models—Chevy Equinox EV, Ford Mustang Mach-E, Hyundai IONIQ 5, and Volkswagen ID.4—are described as affordable options with varying range and trim recommendations to help buyers choose among them.
items.title: Four Used EV SUVs Under $25,000

items.summary: The Malta-flagged Agioi Fanendes, billed as the first tanker carrying Russian ultra-low-sulfur diesel under Trump's deal with Putin, abandoned its planned November 7 arrival in New York after idling off Denmark. Senator Richard Blumenthal demanded it be recalled from U.S. ports on October 28, arguing Congress—not Treasury—must authorize such imports. With no declared destination and banks warned away, the vessel could redirect to Cuba.
items.title: Trump-era Russian diesel tanker drops New York, may head to Cuba

items.summary: The U.S. Energy Information Administration says natural gas production is on track to hit a record high, with dry output set to rise to 112.2 billion cubic feet per day from 107.64 bcfd last year (s7). Demand for data center power and surging LNG exports amid expanding capacity are driving the increase as producers scale operations nationwide.
items.title: US Natural Gas Output Set for Record in 2026

items.summary: On October 28, Microsoft forecast fiscal second-quarter cloud growth and overall sales that beat Wall Street estimates, sending shares up more than 5 per cent in after-hours trading. The company generated $18.6 billion in free cash flow in its fiscal first quarter ended September — some $10 billion more than analysts expected — as capital spending came in below the company's own forecast and Azure surged 48 per cent. Microsoft expects second-quarter Azure growth of 49 to 50 per cent, above analyst estimates of 47.6 per cent, according to Visible Alpha data.
items.title: Microsoft's Cloud Growth and Cash Flow Ease AI Spending Fears

items.summary: On Wednesday, Alphabet missed Wall Street profit and revenue expectations while accelerated AI spending worsened its cash burn, sending shares down more than 10 per cent in extended trading. The company reported negative free cash flow of $9.07 billion versus near breakeven estimates, a loss driven by AI research costs. CFO Anat Ashkenazi said capex would rise significantly in 2027 and warned of margin pressure from third-party cloud capacity.
items.title: Alphabet Shares Fall After Revenue Miss and Rising AI Cash Burn

items.summary: Alphabet's stock fell 7% in after-hours trading Wednesday as the company missed profit projections and raised its third-quarter AI spending past $50 billion. The cash burn reinforced investor concerns that hyperscalers are not generating enough revenue to justify debt-funded infrastructure, while Microsoft shares rose on stronger cloud results.
items.title: Alphabet Stock Falls After Earnings Miss and Record AI Spending

items.summary: The Korea Media and Communications Commission fined Google and Apple a combined 63.7 billion won on Wednesday, according to The Associated Press. It said the companies misused their dominant position in app store markets by forcing domestic developers onto proprietary billing and delaying approvals without clear explanations.
items.title: Korea Fines Google and Apple Over App Store Rules

items.summary: Apple announced a touchscreen MacBook Pro carrying a tandem OLED display it calls PROLED XDR, M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, an in-panel touch sensor, Dynamic Island, a 12MP camera and macOS 27. The line comes in 14.2-inch and 16.3-inch sizes with entry prices of $2,899 for the 14-inch model with the M5 Pro chip and $4,799 for the 16-inch model with the M5 Max chip, according to Apple; all figures are U.S. starting prices. Touch models carry a $400 premium over equivalent non-touch versions, though Apple did not list those base prices. Preorders opened Oct. 28, 2026, with deliveries scheduled for Nov. 6, 2026.
items.title: Apple Unveils Touchscreen MacBook Pro at $2,899

items.summary: Businesses questioned whether Budget measures would meaningfully help them, despite the Treasury saying import-tariff removal could save a typical household about £21 a year on food. Morgan Austin of Burgerism welcomed cheaper gherkins but said rising minimum wage and National Insurance had cost her business about £150,000 annually. Gavin Williams argued UK-based suppliers meant zero benefit for his coffee shop, calling the impact nothing.
items.title: Hospitality firms doubt tariff cuts will ease their costs

items.summary: Chancellor John Healey raised taxes on banks and landlords in his first budget to fund a £100 winter handout sent to 20 million English households in council tax bands A-D. The £2.6bn cost includes funding for Scottish and Welsh governments, which he hoped would run similar schemes. He blamed global economic storms, including the war in Iran driving up oil and gas prices, for a grim outlook. Critics argued the support was poorly targeted while savers faced higher taxes and rents could rise. Meanwhile, official forecasts warned of virtually no growth in disposable income by 2030-31 as inflation rises to almost 4%. Bond markets remained unruffled despite higher-than-expected borrowing against Labour's fiscal rules.
items.title: Healey's Budget Taxes Banks and Landlords for Winter Handout

items.summary: The Office for Budget Responsibility's latest forecast flags soaring energy prices as the biggest near-term risk to the UK economy, cutting its growth prediction for next year from 1.6% to 1%. Chancellor John Healey announced policies offering households
items.title: OBR Warns UK Economy Faces Grim Outlook Amid Energy Shock

items.summary: The US Federal Reserve kept interest rates unchanged on Wednesday during its final board meeting before the midterm elections, leaving them at a range of 3.75% to 4%, one of the highest pre-election levels seen in over 20 years. Two of the 12 board members voted against the pause and preferred raising rates by a quarter point. Inflation has remained above 3% for most of this year, up from 3.4% in August to 3.7% in September, while Fed officials cite supply shocks tied to conflict in the Middle East as a key driver. Fed chair Kevin Warsh said politics played no role in the decision and that incoming information will guide future policy. Economists Nicholas Economides and Christopher Waller noted the election may limit radical action and that rate hikes alone cannot address inflation from supply factors.
items.title: Fed Holds Rates Steady in Pre-Midterm Decision Amid Inflation Concerns

items.summary: India is expanding diesel production capacity from 2027 as state-run refiners increase output, potentially strengthening its role in global fuel markets amid geopolitical disruptions. Indian state refiners will collectively add around 16.5 million tonnes per year of diesel capacity in 2027, industry officials said, as the country seeks greater involvement in international refined-fuel trade while conflicts disrupt supply flows.
items.title: India Plans Major Diesel Capacity Expansion by 2027

items.summary: Leading PC makers are moving some production back to China as costs rise, according to the article. HP had planned a “China+1” strategy shifting more than half of its production overseas but is reversing course amid surging memory and storage chip prices driven by AI demand. Analysts expect continued returns despite Western protectionism risks.
items.title: HP Reverses China+1 Plan Amid Chip Cost Surge

items.summary: Amit Setia of Capri Loans Car Platform advises buyers earning ₹80,000 a month to budget for a car from cash flow rather than the loan amount offered. He says total monthly repayments should stay around 30-40% of take-home income, or roughly ₹24,000-₹32,000, leaving only ₹4,000-₹12,000 after a home-loan EMI of ₹20,000. Buyers should also cover fuel, insurance and maintenance before borrowing.
items.title: Loan Expert Advises ₹80,000 Earners on Realistic Car Budget

items.summary: The non-profit group Distributed Denial of Secrets said it released data on more than 40,000 Department of Homeland Security employees, including officials in surveillance and human intelligence. The disclosure draws on information from an entity calling itself the Department of Peace, which harvested details from Okta’s sign-on service used by DHS. Reuters could not fully verify the trove but matched some records to credit bureau data.
items.title: Nonprofit Leaks Data on DHS Employees

items.summary: CBS News editor-in-chief Bari Weiss spoke publicly for the first time about declining ratings at 60 Minutes, saying diminished viewership was not her top priority. She told an industry conference organized by The Information that she could never build anything if focused on the precise number of people tuning in to the show's second feature each Sunday. Overall, she said the program was doing 'tremendously well', though recent episodes drew 5.64 million viewers compared with a season average of 9.1 million.
items.title: Bari Weiss Deflects Criticism Over Falling Ratings

items.summary: Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who landed in Miami on Wednesday after losing the presidential runoff to Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva by more than four million votes, said it was never his intention to "leave my homeland". He described departing from a regime of exception and called himself a victim of a coup d'état. His arrival ended days of speculation about his whereabouts following reports he had crossed into Argentina on Tuesday night local time. Flight tracking data verified by the BBC placed him boarding a private jet at Puerto Iguazú before arriving in Miami, where photographers swarmed as his team shielded him with umbrellas.
items.title: Flávio Bolsonaro denies fleeing Brazil after landing in Miami

items.summary: An eight-year-old girl was seriously injured with head injuries after a wolf attack inside an enclosure at the Johannismühle wildlife park near Baruth/Mark, Brandenburg. She was there with a staff member and two other children when police said the incident occurred Wednesday before opening; she was flown to hospital by helicopter while no one else was hurt. The park is temporarily closed and set to reopen on 2 November. German newspaper Bild reported details as an ongoing investigation continues amid recent European attacks.
items.title: Girl seriously injured in wolf attack at German wildlife park

items.summary: Brazilian right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro landed in Miami with his family on Wednesday and declared himself the rightful leader of Brazil after refusing to concede Sunday's election defeat. He previously fled Brazil following a Supreme Court order over passport handover but traveled using Italian citizenship. The electoral authority confirmed the vote was conducted normally, while Trump declined comment.
items.title: Flavio Bolsonaro Arrives in Miami, Claims Leadership of Brazil

items.summary: Spain's transport minister says a Wednesday rail collision in Castilla-La Mancha that killed at least 68 people followed an order to run despite a technical failure. The findings may revive safety questions after a January high-speed crash killed 46.
items.title: Spanish Transport Minister Says Rail Crash Followed Faulty 'Error' Order

items.summary: Questions are being raised about Spain's rail safety as authorities launch an official investigation into Wednesday's high-speed train collision, which killed at least 68 people and wounded around 100 more. The transport minister said the Renfe service was authorised to proceed despite an active red signal ahead of a stationary Iryo train; Oscar Puente added that the red signal came from a computer communications failure but an erroneous decision restarted it. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez called the event a terrible tragedy and vowed to strengthen safety, while noting the two crashes appeared unrelated. The crash is Europe's deadliest since 2013, following another January accident in which 46 people died.
items.title: Spain launches probe after second fatal high-speed rail crash in a year

items.summary: Bega Group, one of Australia's largest dairy processors, has asked Atherton Tablelands and Far North Queensland dairy farmers to increase deliveries to its Malanda factory by up to 30 per cent. Chief executive Pete Findlay said the company takes about 30 million litres a year from tablelands farmers and would like to reach around 35 or 40 million, while seasonal disruptions may require it to bring in between 1 million and 2 million litres annually from Victoria. Eric Danzi of eastAUSmilk welcomed the request but said sustainable growth likely needs higher pricing, such as a 10 cents-a-litre increase, plus reintroduction of the diesel levy.
items.title: Bega Group asks Far North Queensland farmers for more milk

items.summary: A man in his 40s was seriously injured after three pit bulls attacked him in Broome on October 21. A couple driving past heard his calls for help and used their car to fend off the dogs before driving him to hospital; he was discharged Tuesday evening, a Department of Health spokesperson said. The Shire of Broome says the animals have been euthanased and the incident is under investigation.
items.title: Broome couple rescued man mauled by pit bulls, left rattled

items.summary: Pedestrians passing Tokyo Midtown Hibiya on the afternoon of Oct. 26 may have mistaken a crowd-control scene for construction, with staff directing people into two lanes past temporary walls and yellow signs. The setup marked the red carpet for the opening of the 39th Tokyo International Film Festival (TIFF). Hundreds watched celebrities walk the carpet from around 3 p.m., many carrying TIFF-branded umbrellas after an all-afternoon downpour, before leaving quickly.
items.title: Fans confused by red carpet at Tokyo film festival opening

items.summary: The Point hosts Rong Ying, Fabien Pacory and Remi Piet to discuss a wave of demonstrations sweeping from France to Italy and Albania. Clashes between demonstrators and police have raised questions about the roots of public discontent in Europe. The guests examine the forces behind the unrest and what it means for European governments' political and social landscape.
items.title: Experts examine what is driving Europe's wave of protests

items.summary: The UN General Assembly again called for ending the US embargo on Cuba, but support fell to its lowest level in more than 30 years. The resolution passed with 130 countries in favour, 17 against and 25 abstentions — the weakest margin since 1995. Germany, Italy and Latvia abstained for the first time in 34 years.
items.title: UN Vote Against US Cuba Embargo Hits 30-Year Low

items.summary: José Luis Centella, president of the Communist Party of Spain, discusses how the Communist Party of China has sustained a century-long commitment to long-term planning, innovation-driven growth, and discipline. He offers his perspective on what enables this enduring capacity for reform, though he does not present these views as established fact but rather as an interpretation worth considering.
items.title: Centella on China's Communist Party and its reform drive

items.summary: On November 3, United States citizens vote in midterms held at the midpoint of presidential cycles. Voters choose all House seats and a third of Senate seats, plus governors in many states; results do not decide the White House but heavily influence Congress. Republicans hold slim majorities in both chambers, with observers expecting Democrats to take the House after only four more wins out of 435 races. Analyst Miles Coleman of the Center for Politics at the University of Virginia says midterms are often a referendum on the president, noting Trump's approval is at a record low and that Democrat James Talarico trails Republican Ken Paxton in Texas.
items.title: How US midterm elections shape Trump's presidency

items.summary: Belgium's Federal Public Service Finance (FOD Financiën) announced that a cyberattack disrupted its digital services, prompting the temporary shutdown of the online tax portal MyMinfin and several other services as a precaution. Officials stated they are investigating and securing their systems while extending some affected tax filing deadlines with new dates to be announced. The agency reported no indications so far that personal data was breached or compromised, though it remains under investigation.
items.title: Belgium's Finance Agency Reports Cyberattack on Tax Portal

items.summary: Palestinian citizens of Israel welcomed strong preliminary election results for Arab parties, expressing optimism about change in their community. Residents from Nazareth praised the outcomes and called on elected officials to address violence, crime, education, and jobs. Crime remained a central concern, with one organization reporting 186 crime-related killings in Arab communities through early 2026.
items.title: Palestinian Israeli Voters Hope Arab Party Gains Bring Change

items.summary: Georges-Louis Bouchez, president of Belgium's French-speaking Reformist Movement (MR), told Anadolu that Europe must pursue economic and political reforms and strengthen partnerships with countries such as Türkiye to preserve living standards and maintain global competitiveness. Speaking during a visit to Ankara, he said widespread public dissatisfaction across Europe reflected significant change and urged short-term sacrifices in taxes and social security for efficiency. He called for a pragmatic win-win deal on investment, market access and visas, arguing that the EU should chart a third way between Washington and Beijing amid growing rivalry. Bouchez warned of declining industrial share of GDP over roughly two decades and stressed Europe needs more sovereignty.
items.title: Belgian Party Leader Urges European Reform and Closer Ties With Türkiye

items.summary: Two studies from Guildford, Surrey show that green spaces cool areas and cut noise and pollution with greater detail than earlier research. A walking sensor study in summer 2023 found Stoke Park cooled by an average of 0.2° Celsius per 100 meters inward while dropping noise about 10 decibels; temperatures warmed more than 0.5° C beyond the edge. Fixed sensors across green and blue sites over summers 2023 to 2025 showed woodlands avoided heat waves, and tree shade ran an average of 2.5° C cooler with thermal comfort up to 8.5° C lower. Prashant Kumar of the University of Surrey noted prior work focused on single benefits; Leslie Brandt of Bolton & Menk stressed cooling people rather than places for climate-resilient design.
items.title: Guildford Living Lab Studies Reveal Fine-Scale Benefits of Urban Green Spaces

items.summary: The UN Independent International Fact-Finding Mission for the Sudan said Wednesday that foreign weapons, technology and personnel continue to fuel the war. Chair Mohamed Chande Othman stated investigators found reasonable grounds to believe external transfer of support sustains the conflict, while noting they have not yet linked neighboring states as responsible governments. The mission urged stronger international action and called for expanding the arms embargo beyond Darfur, alongside extending the ICC mandate. It reported grave risks in El Obeid and civilian suffering amid a deepening humanitarian crisis.
items.title: UN Fact-Finding Mission Blames External Actors for Sudan War, Urges Arms Embargo Expansion

items.summary: Binary prediction-market bets on high-profile IPOs are reshaping how retail investors speculate, according to a report citing Michael Ashley Schulman of Cerity Partners. Interest in Anthropic's upcoming listing has generated more than a dozen Polymarket markets covering its fundraising, exchange and valuation, while Kalshi draws similar bets. The filing could value the AI lab between $1.5 trillion and $2 trillion.
items.title: Prediction markets intensify speculation around Anthropic IPO

items.summary: Amazon announced a second round of layoffs this month, eliminating no more than 250 software development jobs, according to Reuters. A spokesperson said the cuts aim to help Amazon operate more efficiently and align with its product roadmap. The company had cut about 16,000 jobs in January 2026 and previously laid off 14,000 employees in October 2025. Other tech firms also reduced staff this week: Microsoft offered voluntary exits to about 60,000 employees, and Dropbox planned cuts of 9% of its global workforce.
items.title: Amazon Cuts Roles Amid Broader Tech Layoffs

items.summary: A federal judge in San Jose, California, ordered the Trump administration to stop enforcing a Pentagon ban barring defense business with companies that lobby for Alibaba. The ruling tested Washington's ability to limit Chinese firms' activities but did not address Alibaba's separate challenge to its placement on the 1260H list added June 8. Bloomberg News reported the case as closely watched amid US-China rivalry.
items.title: Alibaba Wins Ruling on Lobbying Ban Tied to US Blacklisting

items.summary: BJP-led NDA won 16 of 28 seats in MLC polls across Karnataka, Bihar, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh, sweeping all four Karnataka constituencies. BJP led UP as counting continued from Tuesday to late Wednesday; it took six declared seats there while SP gained three. Congress conceded organisational weaknesses, with D K Shivakumar noting they expected two Karnataka seats but fell short.
items.title: NDA Wins MLC Polls, Congress Falters

items.summary: Congress MP Rahul Gandhi attacked the government over how the Tatas are being handled at Bombay House, saying business leaders stay silent while Indian business is not a plaything of Modi and Amit Shah. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman rebuked him for politicising commercial matters and accusing Congress of harming business interests. Gandhi then questioned why Tata entities were hosted at Amit Shah's residence. The exchange continued across social media posts, with both sides accusing each other of spreading distrust toward Indian industry. No figures or dates appear in the item beyond rhetorical references to 'crony number 1' and '3-4 cronies'.
items.title: Congress MP and Finance Minister Trade Blows Over Tata Case

items.summary: Apple introduced a new 24-inch iMac and an entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro, both powered by the M6 chip that first appeared in the Mac mini in September. The updates are largely internal; Apple said the iMac is five times faster for AI than its 2024 model, while the MacBook Pro is 30% faster on graphics. Both machines start at $1,499 and $1,999 respectively, with preorders opening Wednesday and sales beginning Nov. 6.
items.title: Apple Unveils M6 iMac and Entry MacBook Pro in Computer Lineoverhaul

items.summary: On Wednesday, Punjab Jail Minister Ravjot Singh inaugurated the Women's Open Air Jail at Central Jail Patiala during the Ujala Punjab Prison Olympics 2026. The event included tug-of-war and kabaddi matches plus Giddha and Bhangra performances. Addressing attendees, Ravjot Singh said the Bhagwant Mann-led government promotes sports, fitness and cultural activities in prisons to encourage positive mindsets and help inmates reintegrate into society after release.
items.title: Punjab Jail Minister Inaugurates Women's Open Air Jail in Patiala

items.summary: US Vice President JD Vance sent a letter to Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council and former IRGC commander, in an effort to revive peace talks with Tehran. The outreach came at the direction of President Donald Trump, who is threatening renewed military strikes ahead of next week’s US midterm elections. Diplomacy has yet to produce a detailed proposal as both sides remain divided over nuclear concessions and economic relief.
items.title: Vance Opens Backchannel to Iran Hard-liner as Trump Threatens Strikes

items.summary: Congress leader Abhijeet Govindrao Vanjari won the Nagpur Division Graduates' constituency seat in the Maharashtra Legislative Council for a second consecutive term. A lawyer and educationist, he first took the seat in 2020 as a Maha Vikas Aghadi candidate by more than 18,000 votes, ending a Bharatiya Janata Party stronghold.
items.title: Congress's Abhijeet Vanjari Wins Second Term in Nagpur Graduates' Seat

items.summary: Brazilian senator Flávio Bolsonaro declared himself the country's "true president-elect," alleging fraud in Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's re-election and vowing to lead opposition from the United States. He rejected his departure as a flight, thanking Donald Trump and Javier Milei for support. The statement offered no evidence of electoral fraud, though he claimed Lula gained over 10 million votes.
items.title: Flávio Bolsonaro Declares Himself Brazil's True President-Elect From US

items.summary: Veteran federal judge Alvin Hellerstein, age 92, died Wednesday surrounded by family. He presided over high-profile cases including the Maduro narco-terrorism trial and Sept. 11 litigation. Chief Judge Laura Swain praised his distinguished service. His sentencing of Bill Hwang to 18 years drew public comments about faith and justice.
items.title: Federal Judge Alvin Hellerstein Dies at 92 After High-Profile Cases

items.summary: A guide for Dhanteras and Diwali travellers explains that strong demand and higher operating costs have pushed one-way fares up sharply this festive season, with a report by The Economic Times citing rises of 68% year-on-year on the Delhi-Hyderabad route and 51% on Mumbai-Kolkata. Cleartrip recommends booking two to three months ahead, tracking fares over the previous 30 days, using date flexibility, and comparing bank offers before purchasing, while noting that historical trends are not a guarantee of lower prices. For trains, it points out heavy demand around festivals and suggests checking reservation windows as they open. The article ends with a disclaimer that it does not guarantee cheaper tickets.
items.title: Cleartrip Guides Festive Travellers on Cheaper Flights and Trains

items.summary: Adani Airport Holdings Ltd (AAHL) said a couple of international airlines may temporarily suspend Mumbai services rather than relocate to Navi Mumbai International Airport, according to AAHL CEO Arun Bansal during Adani Enterprises’ earnings call on Wednesday. The airline suspensions could last about two years as Terminal 1 redevelopment begins in April 2027. Airlines opposed unilateral slot cuts and requested phased terminal work; officials asked them to share transition plans by November 3, but airlines sought more time.
items.title: Adani Airport CEO Warns Some Airlines May Halt Mumbai Flights for Two Years
